questions.question: Q: Find the mode, median, and mean of: 3, 5, 5, 7, 10
questions.correctAnswer: Mode = 5 (appears twice). Median = 5 (middle value of 5 numbers). Mean = (3 + 5 + 5 + 7 + 10) ÷ 5 = 30 ÷ 5 = 6.

questions.question: Q: A student scores 65, 70, and 75 in tests weighted 2, 3, and 5 respectively. Calculate the weighted mean.
Q: An investment grows by 10% in year 1 and 20% in year 2. Why is the geometric mean more appropriate than the arithmetic mean for the average growth rate?
questions.correctAnswer: Growth is multiplicative, so the geometric mean = √(1.10 × 1.20) = √1.32 ≈ 1.149, giving an average growth rate of about 14.9%. The arithmetic mean (15%) would overestimate the overall growth.

questions.question: Q: A dataset has values 2, 3, 3, 3, 100. Explain why the median is more appropriate than the mean.
questions.correctAnswer: The outlier 100 pulls the mean to 22.2, which does not represent the data well. The median of 3 better reflects the central value since most data are around 3.

questions.question: Full-Mark Response The table shows the number of siblings for 30 students. Calculate the estimated mean. 0–1: frequency 8, 2–3: frequency 14, 4–5: frequency 6, 6–7: frequency 2 <div class="
questions.correctAnswer: Find midpoints and calculate f × midpoint: Class | Midpoint (m) | f | f × m 0–1 | 0.5 | 8 | 4 2–3 | 2.5 |14 | 35 4–5 | 4.5 | 6 | 27 6–7 | 6.5 | 2 | 13 Total | |30 | 79 Estimated mean = Σ(f × m) ÷ Σf = 79 ÷ 30 = 2.63 (to 2 d.p.) This is an estimate because we have used midpoints rather than the actual data values within each class.
